description: Laravel Telescope-inspired debugging and monitoring for NestJS. Watchers record requests, queries, exceptions, logs, jobs, cache, events, mail, GraphQL and more, shown in a real-time dashboard mounted in the application, with in-memory, SQLite or Redis storage and an MCP server that lets AI agents read what was recorded.
rules: Call NestLensModule.forRoot() once, in the root module. It is global: feature modules inject CollectorService or a watcher such as GateWatcher without importing NestLensModule.
An application that imports NestLensModule but never calls forRoot() fails at startup with an error saying so: nothing would configure it.
The dashboard is served at the path option, /nestlens by default (http://localhost:3000/nestlens), and its REST API under <path>/__nestlens__/api.
Storage is in memory by default and lost on restart. driver: 'sqlite' needs better-sqlite3 installed; driver: 'redis' needs ioredis.
The dashboard and API answer only when NODE_ENV is development, local or test (authorization.allowedEnvironments), but recording runs wherever enabled is true: gate enabled by environment.
Before allowing NestLens in another environment, configure authorization.allowedIps or authorization.canAccess, and read the production usage guide.
The GraphQL watcher is off by default. With watchers: { graphql: true } it registers itself with Apollo or Mercurius; no plugin wiring is needed.
Bull and BullMQ queues are recorded after jobWatcher.setupQueue(queue, name); Prisma model entries after modelWatcher.setupPrismaClient(client). TypeORM is found on its own.

AI agents read NestLens through the nestlens-mcp package. Its --url is the application address plus the mount path, such as http://localhost:3000/nestlens. It is read-only unless --allow-write is set.
